🧠 A few early exits can make winning trades barely outsize losing ones, making consistent profits harder to achieve.

Why? That open profit starts to feel like money you might lose. You picture the regret of watching it vanish, so closing the trade brings instant relief. It may look like careful management, but sometimes it’s simply a way to escape the discomfort of holding on.

Before your next trade, rehearse both choices: close or hold. Then ask whether fear of losing your unrealized gain is making the decision for you.

One way to practise is to split your planned position in two: close one part and leave the other open. It can make holding winners less uncomfortable, though it doesn’t remove the risk.

📌 Bridges and Cross-Chain Swaps: Where Hacks Happen

Main Points
⏺ Cross-chain services hold large pools of user funds in shared vaults
⏺ When their keys or code fail, liquidity providers take the loss
⏺ This post explains the risk and how to limit your exposure



1️⃣ Core Idea — A bridge or cross-chain swap does not move your coins between chains. It locks them in a vault on one side and pays you out on the other. Whoever controls that vault controls the money.
2️⃣ Why It Happens — Vaults are run by signing keys, validators or smart contracts. If any of them is compromised, an attacker can drain everything at once.
3️⃣ Example — Over the weekend Chainflip lost about $12 million, including 122.86 BTC, after a suspected compromise of its signing key. Its services were paused.
4️⃣ Risk Surface — Liquidity you deposit in bridge pools, swaps left pending mid-route, unlimited token approvals, and fake "recovery" sites that appear after every hack.
5️⃣ Practical Rule — Use bridges only to move funds, not to store them. Swap, confirm arrival, revoke approvals, and keep only what you can afford to lose in cross-chain pools.
Final Thoughts

Bridges are useful, but they concentrate risk. Treat every cross-chain step as a short trip, not a place to park your crypto.

I have to tell you something, and many of you are not going to like it. In fact, I am going to be attacked in the comments for even writing this.

For the past 11 years, including these past three years as Israel fought this existential war, Netanyahu has faced investigations and legal proceedings involving many serious allegations, including bribery.

He has been saying from day one that, in the end, the courts will discover that he did nothing wrong.

And yet, my feed for over a decade has been full of people telling me how corrupt Bibi is and how he’s guilty of so many things.

After all, they said, where there’s smoke, there’s fire!

He’s not being accused of all these things for nothing, they said!

Well, allow me to tell you what just happened, because it’s unbelievable!

Netanyahu’s judges just told the attorney general what many have suspected:

Cases 4000 and 2000 are falling apart!

In remarks to the AG after Netanyahu finished his testimony, the judges said that the trial has reached a juncture where “the public interest requires reconsideration.”

Case 4000 (bribery): The quid pro quo rests mainly on Shlomo Filber’s testimony. The judges reportedly said that it is hard to base findings on it, given his shifting accounts and objective evidence that contradicts him.

They also have serious doubts about whether “exceptional responsiveness” to Bezeq was proven or whether Netanyahu knew about it at the time.

Even the breach of trust charge is reportedly in trouble. In their view, the chance of a conviction is low enough to justify reconsidering the case.

Their reported recommendation is to consider dropping the charge.

Yep, you read that right.

Case 2000 (Mozes): The judges reportedly have serious doubts about whether the conduct described in the indictment constitutes a crime at all. They want to hear legal arguments before deciding how to proceed.

Case 1000 (gifts, including a Bugs Bunny doll): Most of the evidence is already in. They want to move toward a verdict.

The judges stressed that they have not written a verdict. But as former Deputy AG Raz Nizri reportedly told his colleagues at the State Attorney’s Office: “You have golden evidence; the only problem is that there is no crime.”

Yeah, so 11 years of nonstop accusations and division over these cases. I don’t even want to know how much money has been spent on these proceedings, in addition to all the time invested.

While trying to conduct and win this war, Netanyahu has had to repeatedly appear in court to refute what are ridiculous and false accusations.

Now that even the judges are reportedly expressing serious doubts about these cases, what we should do is figure out who was behind these accusations in the first place and why these proceedings have gone on for as long as they have.

Here’s the thing, though.

Remember how the whole country went nuts over the judicial reform? Remember how one side said that the reform would be the end of democracy, while the other side said that the judicial system had way too much power and needed reform?

Well, in my view, what we’re seeing now illustrates exactly why reform is necessary.

A judicial system that has spent years and millions upon millions in an attempt to bring Bibi down at all costs??

That is not normal. None of this is normal.

Someone should he held accountable for this and if you ask me, it’s the attorney general who has weaponized the judicial system to meet her political agenda and has been caught multiple times including leaking that doctored video of IDF soldiers abusing Palestinians, something that never happened and caused Israel immense and irreversible damage. 

She should be behind bars for that and for this!

Now we wait to see whether the rest of the cases against Bibi fall apart, because that’s exactly what I believe is going to happen!

Go ahead call me a “Bibist”. Call me whatever you want. It won’t change the fact that one by one, the accusations against Bibi are falling apart.

(Hillel Fuld on X)

11,000 Messages. Still No Clear Picture.

Microsoft sells workplace coordination. During its Nov. 12 and 13 outage, engineers exchanged more than 11,000 messages across 11 Teams chats and still struggled to assemble a coherent picture of the crisis, internal memos reviewed by Reuters show.

The roughly 24-hour failure disrupted Microsoft 365 services, including Exchange Online, Outlook, Teams, and Copilot. Governments lost service, trading firms faced delays and airline communications suffered. Microsoft called it Exchange Online’s most customer-impacting incident ever.

The company blamed an undetected Windows scaling defect introduced in July, ruling out a cyberattack or AI agents. Diagnostic data sat in fragmented tracking systems. In a separate incident, an urgent fix took five to six days to deploy worldwide.
